The story is a deeply original piece of literary fiction that avoids cliched expressions, stock characters, and predictable plot tropes. Instead of relying on overused phrases, the author crafts fresh, specific similes and metaphors—such as people walking in the rain "like men carrying invisible planks," a leek poking out of a grocery bag "like a green flag," and an imagined laugh sounding "like a log settling in a grate." Furthermore, the central premise—a narrator drawing an eerie, poetic parallel between a half-burned armchair left on the curb and a woman he follows home during a slow-rising flood—is unconventional and unpredictable, steering clear of any melodramatic or formulaic resolutions.
